name: Wing Loong II
operator: PLA; widely exported (UAE, Saudi Arabia, Egypt, others)
overview_md:
The Wing Loong II ("Pterodactyl II") is China's flagship medium-altitude long-endurance (MALE) armed drone and its principal competitor to the U.S. MQ-9 Reaper in the global market. Built by Chengdu, it is a turboprop-powered hunter-killer UAV that pairs persistent surveillance with a meaningful strike payload — and, crucially, a price tag well below its American rival.

With an endurance of roughly 20–32 hours, twelve hardpoints and an external payload of around 480 kg, the Wing Loong II carries laser-guided bombs and Blue Arrow air-to-ground missiles, controlled by satellite datalink for beyond-line-of-sight operations. Its sensor turret and synthetic-aperture radar provide the ISR backbone for both reconnaissance and strike.

For an analyst, the Wing Loong's significance is as much commercial and political as military. Because U.S. export rules long restricted sales of armed Reapers, China stepped into the gap, selling armed drones across the Middle East, Africa and Asia and accumulating combat experience through its operators in Libya, Yemen and elsewhere. In the Indo-Pacific and beyond, the Wing Loong is a tool of Chinese defence diplomacy and a driver of armed-drone proliferation — reshaping who has access to persistent precision strike.

combat_history.event: Wing Loong drones operated by foreign customers saw combat in Libya and Yemen.
combat_history.significance: Gave Chinese armed-drone designs real combat exposure via exports.

modernization.description: Higher-performance and jet-powered Wing Loong derivatives broaden the export range.
modernization.impact: Sustains China's lead in the armed-drone export market.

vulnerabilities.description: Slow, non-stealthy MALE drone vulnerable to modern air defences and fighters.
vulnerabilities.context: Restricted to permissive or lightly-defended airspace.
vulnerabilities.mitigation: Used for ISR/strike where air defence is weak.

vulnerabilities.description: Relies on a jam-able satellite control link.

operational_patterns.typical_deployment: Persistent ISR and precision strike in permissive airspace; widely operated by export customers.
operational_patterns.typical_task_group: Operated via satellite control; networked into customer C2.

peer_comparisons.key_differences: The Reaper has greater endurance, payload and a more mature sensor suite; the Wing Loong undercuts it on price and export availability.
peer_comparisons.video_angle: Reaper vs Wing Loong — the armed-drone export war.

peer_comparisons.key_differences: TB2 is smaller and cheaper still; the Wing Loong sits between TB2 and Reaper.
GJ-11 is a stealthy UCAV for contested airspace; Wing Loong is a permissive-airspace workhorse.
peer_comparisons.video_angle: China's two faces of unmanned strike.

doctrine.role: Medium-altitude long-endurance armed ISR drone for persistent surveillance and strike — and a flagship export.
doctrine.employment: Satellite-controlled day-long sorties for reconnaissance and precision strike in permissive airspace.
doctrine.design_philosophy: Reaper-class capability at a fraction of the price, available for export.
doctrine.threat_context: Drives armed-drone proliferation and Chinese defence diplomacy across the Indo-Pacific and beyond.
doctrine.comparison_frame: Read against the MQ-9, Turkey's TB2 and China's own stealthy GJ-11.
